correctness.rationale: For any finite connected simple \(H\) with at least two vertices, the clique-fiber Laplacian splits as \(L_H\otimes I+I\otimes mP_1\). Its pseudoinverse gives \(R_{\mathrm{horizontal}}=q/m+(1-1/m)h\), with \(q\le1\) and \(h=b^{\mathsf T}(L_H+mI)^{-1}b\le2/(m+2)\) by positive-matrix inverse order; \(R_{\mathrm{vertical}}=2(S_m)_{xx}<2/m\). Thus for \(m\ge4\) every diagonal is at most \(3/(m+2)\), strictly smaller for \(H\ne K_2\). For any orthogonal edge projector \(Q\) and \(C=I-Q\), each column satisfies \(\|C\delta_e\|_1=\|Q\delta_e\|_1+1-2Q_{ee}\). Taking maxima proves the sharp norm gap; direct two-orbit rational formulas for \(K_2\) show equality for all \(m\ge4\), and the \(m=3\) case violates the universal direction. The exact transfer-current formulas and \(m(L_H+mI)^{-1}\to I\) prove both fixed-base endpoint limits. Standalone standard-library rational checks compared independent full-product and compressed constructions. No quantitative assertion relies on numeric extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The mathematical novelty is the sharp norm difference \((m-4)/(m+2)\), quantified over all finite connected base graphs, its unique equality case, and the two base-dependent large-clique norm limits. The complete 2023 projection paper supplies the cut/cycle framework and Hamming-graph examples but not these assertions. A 1997 graph-product resistance study has a closely related setting, yet its accessible abstract concerns random-walk hitting probabilities instead. Special graph-product examples do not imply the all-base bounds. The inaccessible 1997 full text remains a named comparison risk, not evidence of noncoverage.

value.rationale: The theorem covers every finite connected base graph, rather than isolated examples or numerical constants. It establishes the least clique size guaranteeing nonnegative canonical cut/cycle norm dominance, a sharp quantitative gap attained only by \(K_2\), and two limiting norm laws recovering the invariant \(\|Q_H\|_{1\to1}\) of any fixed base. These structural consequences are motivated by complementability behavior on clique-prism and Hamming examples and inform electrical-flow localization in Banach edge-space decompositions. No minimality among arbitrary projectors or intermediate-exponent formula is asserted.
